title: How Long Would You Last Falling Into Jupiter? #shorts
description_hook: You are dropped at Jupiter's cloud tops at -108 °C, with nothing solid below and no oxygen to breathe. The clock starts now.

beats.say: How long would you last falling into Jupiter? You get dropped at the cloud tops. It's minus 108 degrees Celsius.
beats.img: a lone tiny human silhouette seen from behind tumbling above an endless sea of cream and rust colored cloud bands, a pale distant sun, freezing thin haze

beats.say: Gravity is 2.36 times Earth's. You're suddenly heavy. And there's no ground below. Jupiter has no true surface.
beats.img: looking straight down through layer after layer of swirling ochre clouds into a bottomless dark abyss, no horizon, vertical sense of falling

beats.say: Then the wind finds you. Up to 539 kilometers per hour, flinging you sideways through the clouds.
beats.img: violent streaks of white and orange storm clouds racing sideways past a small falling figure, motion blur, roaring turbulent sky

beats.say: Now breathe. The air is 89.8% hydrogen. No oxygen at all. One or two breaths, and you're unconscious.
beats.img: a glowing outline of a human head and chest fading into soft blue gas, a faint final breath dissolving into dim amber haze

gumi.say: Gumi's odds: zero. NASA's probe lasted 58 minutes, down to 22.7 atmospheres. You won't.
